newsitem.title: LEBANON: Rights group accuses Syrian forces in Lebanon.
newsitem.headline: Rights group accuses Syrian forces in Lebanon.

text.p: A U.S.-based human rights group accused Syrian forces of abducting Lebanese and Palestinians in Lebanon, sometimes with the help of Lebanese security forces, and urged the Beirut government to stop them.

Human Rights Watch said in a 36-page report that detainees seized in Lebanon were taken to Syria and some had been missing for years. Efforts to obtain information about them through the Lebanese judiciary or government met no response.

"An unknown number of Lebanese citizens and stateless Palestinians are imprisoned in Syria: some of them 'disappeared' in Lebanon as long ago as the 1980s," the report said. It called on Syrian President Hafez al-Assad to publish a list of all non-Syrian detainees in his country.
Syria has an estimated 35,000 troops in Lebanon which the Beirut government says help it maintain security in the country.
"The Lebanese government clearly has ceded certain police powers to Syrian intelligence forces inside Lebanon -- in practice if not also by secret agreement," Human Rights Watch said.
Syrian forces maintained detention facilities in at least five places in Lebanon and a joint centre with Lebanese intelligence at Hazmiyeh on the edge of Beirut, it said.
It cited the abductions of two Palestinians this year.

"Lebanese citizens and stateless Palestinians continue to 'disappear' in Lebanon, taken into custody there by Syrian security forces and then transferred to and detained in Syria, perpetuating a climate of fear," it said.
The two Palestinians, held in Januarry and March, were taken to Damascus for interrogation after detention in Beirut and the eastern Bekaa valley. Both were released after several weeks.
The report said Human Right Watch also had first-hand testimony that Syrian forces held Lebanese in detention centres in Lebanon or Syria to pressure them to collaborate with them.

"Human Rights Watch calls on the Lebanese government to take firm and transparent measures to end abuses in Lebanon at the hands of Syrian security forces, and to ensure that Lebanese military and security authorities in no manner participate in or facilitate 'disappearances' on Lebanese soil," the group said.
It urged Lebanon's Prime Minister Rafik al-Hariri and President Elias Hrawi to declare publicly that Syrian forces would not be allowed to operate with impunity in Lebanon.

It also demanded the establishment of a legal regime to discipline and hold the Syrian forces accountable for any crimes they committed in Lebanon and urged the government to order Lebanese forces not to take part in any way in carrying out the "disappearances".
